issues.description: The UML diagram in the problem statement declares the attribute 'lectureName' as type int, but everywhere else (the textual example, required toString output, and the solution implementation) treats 'lectureName' as a String. This contradictory type information can confuse students when they add attributes and implement the constructor/getters/setters and may lead them to choose the wrong type.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare lectureName as type String (lectureName: String) so it matches the example output and the intended implementation. Optionally add a brief note in the description clarifying that lectureName is textual, and ensure the constructor/signatures shown in the UML follow the same types.
